title: What a Friend We Have in Jesus
summary: Jesus calls us friends: on mission together, sharing sweet fellowship, and proven true in times of trouble.
exhortation: It would be an amazing grace beyond our comprehension if God simply saved us and made us his servants. And yet Jesus calls us friends. So what does it mean to be a friend?

Friends are on mission together. As we go through this world and this spiritual battle, proclaiming the gospel, building his church, and teaching and training people, we aren't doing it alone as servants sent out. We do it as friends. Jesus is in the foxhole with us. He is in the battle with us through his Holy Spirit.

Friendship has a sweetness in fellowship: being on the same page, conversations late into the night. If you've had those moments with friends, they're some of the sweetest times of life. We get those times with Jesus.

And a good friend is proven in times of trouble. Hardship is often when you find out who your real friends are, and we find a true friend in Jesus most of all when we're in trouble. So meditate on this as you go through the day. Think of the sweetest times you've had with good friends, and consider what an amazing thing it is to call Jesus, the King of kings and Lord of lords, the God of the universe, our friend.
prayer: What a privilege to call you friend. Lord, thank you for being so near to us. You are not distant and far off. If anything, we are the ones pushing you away and forgetting your nearness. You aren't standing far off, holding things over our heads. You are eager to bring us back and be near us. You paid the ultimate price so that we could be near you.
Help us remember as we go through our day that you are with us. What a friend we have in Jesus. Amen.
